items.content:
Americano

"He is a sharp trader, a savage enemy and an unreliable friend. He has no respect for ideas, and fears them as he derides them. He lacks gallantry, generosity, tolerance, the sense of justice, even common fairness. He is ignorant, callous and bombastic. Facing easy odds, he makes a great show of bellicosity. But he is easy to alarm, and alarmed, he is a coward."

This prophetic description was penned in 1927 by one of my favorites, the Sage of Baltimore, H. L. Mencken, and published in the American Mercury, a magazine founded by Mencken.

Upon reflection, it is a perfect description of a contemporary whose name everyone in the world knows.

As for that contemporary’s name, I will give you three guesses, and the first two don't count.
